text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Engineers to hold sit-in in front of Public Works and Housing Ministry today in escalation of pay dispute.

- Zarqa municipality deputy head says members will resign on Saturday unless prosecutors release Zarqa mayor Mustafa al-Fayad, who was charged over newspaper article describing three quarters of parliamentarians as liars. Fayad has been taken to hospital with irregular heartbeats.
- Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai says in interview criticisms will not deflect Israel from building in East Jerusalem.
- Senior government sources say Jordan is actively seeking approval from United Nations committee for its contracts to export goods to Iraq under the December food-for-oil deal.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to visit Amman tomorrow; Mordechai's visit cancelled.
- Work expected to start in next few months on construction of American University in Jordan in the Red Sea port of Aqaba.
- Islamist Action Front deputy Bassam Namoush says it would be better for IAF to be in coalition with government than in opposition.
- PLO's Farouk Kaddoumi in Amman for talks with Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.
- Jordan has detailed documents of private land ownership rights in Palestine dating back to Ottoman era.
- Israel names Oded Eran, deputy-general of economic affairs at foreign ministry, as new ambassador to Jordan from the end of this month.
- U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Louis Freeh ends visit after talks with King Hussein, Kabariti, and Justice Minister Abdul-Karim al-Dughmi.
